title: improve-token-level-observability-dashboards-and-alert-tuning
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Our token-level cost/latency breakdowns were missing per-route labels and had noisy alert firing during traffic spikes. This PR adds more granular token-level metrics, improves tracing span tags for better attribution, updates Grafana dashboards to surface p50/p95 token-level cost and latency by model+route, and retunes SLO alerts to reduce false positives. Changes are backward-compatible with existing metric names (new labels added) and include rollout guidance and a short validation checklist. Checklist: - [x] Add token-level cost and latency metrics with route/model tags and prefix/kvcache labels - [x] Instrument tracing spans with route_id and model_version attrs and increase default sampling to 5% for high-error routes - [x] Update Grafana dashboard JSON with new panels for per-route token cost/latency and service-level breakdowns - [x] Create alert runbook and adjust thresholds to use adaptive windows (1m, 5m, 15m) and reduce noise on cold-starts - [x] Add unit tests for metric label logic and e2e smoke test for dashboard generation Summary of changes (high level): 1) Metrics: added token_cost_seconds, token_latency_seconds_histogram and token_emitted_count counters tagged with route, model, quantization_profile, kvcache_hit (true|false) and request_priority. Introduced a histogram bucket set optimized for sub-10ms token latencies. 2) Tracing: added consistent span tags (route_id, model_version, shard_id) and a small helper to attach KV cache hit metadata to the generation span. 3) Dashboards: new Grafana dashboard JSON (dashboards/token_cost_latency.json) with panels for per-route token cost breakdown, cost per 1k tokens, p50/p95 token latency heatmaps, and hotspot tables for models/routes with highest per-token cost. 4) Alerts/runbook: moved token-latency alert to use adaptive evaluation windows and added suppression when cold_start=true tag is present for a route. Added a runbook with remediation steps and rollback guidance. 5) Tests: unit tests for metric label formatting and an integration test that emits synthetic traces/metrics and verifies dashboard snapshots. Rollout plan: apply metrics/tracing changes to staging; deploy a canary of the new instrumentation in staging and low-traffic clusters; after 24-48h of stable metrics, roll out to production with a 10% traffic canary and monitor new dashboard panels. Validation: see validation_steps field below for detailed checks. Notes: kept legacy metric names as aliases, added feature flag `observability.token_level_v2` to gate sampling increase. This PR is intended to reduce mean-time-to-detect regressions in model performance and to make cost attribution more accurate for internal chargebacks.

observability/tracing/span_tags.py: +def attach_generation_tags(span, route_id, model_version, shard_id, kvcache_hit):

+    span.set_tag('model_version', model_version)

alerts/token_latency_alerts.yaml: - alert: TokenLatencyHigh
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket{cold_start!="true"}[5m])) by (le, route, model)) > 0.1
  for: 5m
  annotations: {summary: "P95 token latency > 100ms (adjustable)"}
review_comments: Miguel Lopez: Please add a note about cardinality and ensure route+model labels are low-cardinality. Can we map long route names to short ids?
Aisha Patel: Good point, added a route_id label and a mapping layer in token_metrics.py; long route names are preserved as route_name for dashboards only.
Dana Kim: Tests look good but can we add an integration smoke test that verifies dashboard panels render with synthetic data?
Aisha Patel: Added tests/integration/test_dashboard_snapshot.py that runs the snapshot generator against synthetic metrics; CI now validates the dashboard JSON schema.
Evelyn Zhang: Alert thresholds seem aggressive for smaller routes. Suggest using adaptive windows and a suppression during warmup/cold_start.
Aisha Patel: Implemented adaptive windows (1m/5m/15m) and a cold_start tag check to suppress alerts during warmup. Updated runbook with guidance for threshold tuning per-customer tiers.
release_notes: Added token-level cost and latency metrics with per-route and per-model labels, updated Grafana dashboards to show token-level cost/latency breakdowns, and retuned token-latency alerts to reduce false positives during cold starts. Feature gated under observability.token_level_v2. Rollout instructions included in runbook.
validation_steps: Enable feature flag observability.token_level_v2 in staging and deploy the metrics service
Run scripts/dashboard_snapshot_update.sh to generate a dashboard snapshot and commit the JSON to a staging branch
Verify new dashboard panels render in staging Grafana with synthetic metrics (use tests/integration/test_dashboard_snapshot.py)
Smoke test: send synthetic traces with kvcache_hit true/false and confirm spans show route_id and model_version tags
Canary rollout in prod: 10% traffic with metric dashboards observed for 24h, confirm no increase in alert volume
After stable canary, roll out to 100% and monitor cost attribution reports for expected accuracy improvements
